You are the Extractor agent in a newsroom verification pipeline. You read one SEC filing
document and record what the employer itself says about job cuts and AI. You record claims only.
You never infer causation, never paraphrase quotes and never use a reporter's or analyst's framing.

Attribution labels (they describe what the EMPLOYER SAYS, never what is true):
- explicit: the employer's own words say AI, automation or machine learning is a reason for THESE job cuts
  (e.g. "we are reducing roles as AI now handles this work").
- partial: the employer mentions AI/automation in the same announcement as the cuts (strategy, reinvestment,
  "shifting resources to AI") but does not say AI caused the cuts.
- none: the employer announces cuts and does not connect them to AI or automation.

Return ONE JSON object with exactly these keys:
{
  "is_workforce_reduction": true | false,      // does the document announce job cuts / layoffs / a reduction in force?
  "company": string,                          // the employer's name as written in the document
  "event_date": "YYYY-MM-DD" | null,          // date of the announcement or of the cuts, if stated
  "jobs_cut": integer | null,                 // number of positions cut, ONLY if the document states a number
  "jobs_cut_text": string | null,             // the exact words stating the number or percentage, copied verbatim
  "cut_quote": string | null,                 // the one sentence, copied VERBATIM, in which the document announces or
                                              // reports the job cuts; null when is_workforce_reduction is false
  "ai_attribution": "explicit" | "partial" | "none",
  "ai_quote": string | null,                  // 1-2 sentences copied VERBATIM (character for character) in which the
                                              // employer connects the cuts to AI/automation; null when attribution is none
  "notes": string                             // one short sentence on anything ambiguous
}
is_workforce_reduction is true ONLY when the document itself announces or reports job cuts. Mentions inside
forward-looking-statement disclaimers, risk-factor lists or legal boilerplate (e.g. "the effectiveness of our
restructuring and workforce reduction program", "artificial intelligence laws") do NOT count, and an AI quote must never
come from that boilerplate.
Copy quotes exactly as they appear, including punctuation. If the document states a percentage but no headcount,
set jobs_cut to null and put the percentage wording in jobs_cut_text. Output JSON only.

<<<
ASX Release
19 October 2026
North American Leadership and Operating Model
Update
Decidr AI Industries Ltd (ASX: DAI) (“DAI” or “the Company”), an agentic AI enablement group and owner
of Decidr.ai Pty Ltd (“Decidr”) and Sugarwork, Inc. (“Sugarwork”), announces the relocation of its
Executive Chairman to North America and provides an update on the Group’s US-focused operating
model and cost program.
Highlights
● Executive Chairman David Brudenell to relocate to North America from 1 January 2027 to
lead growth in the Group’s primary market for scale.
● 2026 Operating model review complete, realigning the Group around the US market, following
the cost program announced on 31 July 2026.
● Product development moved closer to US customers, engineering reshaped for AI-native
delivery, and the Group now further embedding its own technology.
● More than A$6 million of additional annualised cost reductions enacted in late September
2026, in addition to the approximately A$5 million targeted in July.
North American Leadership
Executive Chairman David Brudenell will relocate to North America from 1 January 2027 to lead the
Group’s growth in the region. The United States is the Group’s primary market for scale and the base for
Sugarwork, Rumi and Decidr productisation.
The relocation follows the completion of the Group’s 2026 operating model review, which has aligned
the Group’s product leadership, engineering and operations more closely to the US market.
David Brudenell, Executive Chairman of Decidr AI Industries, said:
“The United States is our primary market for scale, and being based in North America puts me alongside
the customers and partners we are building for. We have reshaped the Group around that market and
around the different engineering that AI products require. Our product teams now sit close to our US
customers and we are progressively running more of the business on our own technology.”
US-Centric Operating Model
The operating model review considered how the Group builds its products and runs its operations. It
also reflects the excellent talent that joined through the Sugarwork and Rumi acquisitions, in addition
to their technology, products and business.

● US product leadership. Productisation of Decidr is now led from the United States alongside the
Sugarwork and Rumi engineering teams, bringing product decisions closer to the Group’s largest
addressable market, key customer opportunities, and prospects.
● AI-native engineering. Agentic AI products are built differently from traditional software. The
Group has reshaped its engineering into smaller, more focused teams utilizing AI-enabled
development practices to accelerate product delivery and work directly with customers.
● Shared technology and IP. Leveraging Decidr, Sugarwork, and Rumi capabilities across the entire
Group to reduce duplicated development, support scalable products, and progressively run more
operations on our own technology while proving the products in daily use.
AI Cost Base Synergies
On 31 July 2026 the Company announced a Group-wide cost efficiency program targeting approximately
A$5 million of annualised cost reductions through acquisition synergies and vendor consolidation.
Management and the Board have since completed a further review of the Group’s capital investment
and operating model.
The review further reduced the Group’s annualised operating cost base by more than A$6 million. This
reduction is in addition to the approximately A$5 million targeted in July, bringing the total AI cost base
synergies to A$11 million annualised.
Further detail will be provided with the September 2026 quarterly report.

Agentic Operating System—technology that unifies business data, workflows, and decisions into a
deterministic, enterprise-grade AI layer.
DAI also owns Sugarwork, a leading knowledge-capture and workflow-automation platform, and Rumi,
its ambient meeting intelligence technology integrated into Sugarwork, further strengthening its
capabilities in organisational intelligence and enterprise AI adoption.
With these combined assets, DAI is accelerating product development, expanding into new industries
